This is Kenji. He lives in Osaka, he has a Japanese passport, and in May he's flying to Seoul and then on to Vancouver.

His scans are on the family NAS: a photo of his passport, a Korean Air booking, a hotel in Vancouver. What does each country need? The rules sit on official sites in two countries, and he won't upload his passport to a cloud chatbot.
So he asks the assistant on his NAS.

The Skill hands the work to the NAS's own agents. One finds the documents, one reads the passport photo and checks the machine-readable zone, one reads the bookings. Document numbers come back masked, and nothing leaves the NAS.

Then it checks the bundled rules. His passport is fine. Korea needs a K E T A, about ten thousand won, though some nationalities are waived, so he should confirm. Canada needs an E T A, seven Canadian dollars, most approved in minutes, with the official sources and checked dates.
It holds the document lists against his folder. The passport, flights and hotel are there. Neither authorisation is there yet, and nothing shows where he'll stay in Seoul.
Last, a dated plan. Apply for the Canadian E T A now and the K E T A by the twenty-eighth of April, then fly to Seoul on the second of May.
Passport mobility planner. Official rules, checked against your own documents, on your own NAS.
